 Payton Pritchard led the Celtics with 28 points (10-of-16 FGs), one rebound, four assists, two steals and seven three-pointers in a 134-99 win over the Bulls on Monday.
 Pritchard had a rough performance on Friday, where he was held to just four points on 1-of-5 FGs. He surpassed his total for points and three-pointers through their first two games in this game alone. Pritchard is more than capable of producing to this level, though it won’t come consistently. However, he’ll continue to play a significant role off the bench and see plenty of usage.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Payton Pritchard tallied seven points (3-of-11 FGs), three rebounds, 11 assists and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Hornets. 
 Pritchard, who signed a two-year, $44.2 million extension on Tuesday, racked up a game-high 11 assists on Wednesday. He’s coming off his most productive season to date, posting career-best averages in points, rebounds, and assists. Pritchard finished last season as a top-100 player in 12-team formats, and fantasy managers can reasonably expect similar production in 2026-27. 
 Payton Pritchard 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #11 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Payton Pritchard has agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million extension with the Celtics that includes a mutual option in 2029-30. 
 The six-year vet has seen his role blossom from rotational microwave-scorer in Year 1 to key piece of Boston’s 2023-24 title run and 2024-25 Sixth Man of the Year. Pritchard enjoyed the most productive season of his career in 2025-26, posting career-highs with 17 points, 3.9 rebounds and 5.2 assists across 32.6 minutes. Jayson Tatum is back in the mix to open the season, but Pritchard should remain a key scorer and playmaker, and the extension he signed is a reflection of the team’s confidence in him as a foundational franchise player.

 BOS 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Payton Pritchard poured in a game-high 25 points (7-of-12 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), four rebounds and seven assists over 24 minutes in Saturday’s lopsided preseason win over the 76ers. 
 Boston’s bench looked to be in midseason form with Pritchard carrying the bulk of the scoring workload for the non-Tatum unit as he finished the opening half with a team-high 15 points. He drained 5-of-8 attempts from three-point range and finished second on the Celtics behind Jayson Tatum with 12 shot attempts. Pritchard remains a streaky shooter capable of putting up huge scoring numbers when he’s in a groove. He’ll be a top-100 range selection in fantasy drafts this fall. 
 Payton Pritchard 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Payton Pritchard finished Saturday’s Game 7 loss to the 76ers with 13 points (5-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, one steal and two three-pointers. 
 Even with Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla making three changes to his starting lineup for Game 7, Pritchard remained in his usual reserve role. A 2-of-7 night from beyond the arc prevented him from being as impactful as he can be, especially when the three-pointers are falling. Saturday night was a disappointing conclusion to what was, overall, an excellent season for Pritchard. His production picked up once he moved back into the sixth-man role, and that should be Pritchard’s responsibility for 2026-27 with a healthy Jayson Tatum in the fold. Pritchard offers a top-75 fantasy floor, but the ceiling is somewhat limited.

 Payton Pritchard tallied 14 points (6-of-16 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and one three-pointer in the loss to the 76ers on Thursday. 
 Similar to several other Celtics players, Prtichard struggled with his shot in Game 6. He was particularly cold from beyond the arc, which is where half of his field-goal attempts came from. Poor three-point shooting aside, he actually performed offensively, with his five assists being the most for Boston on the night. He’ll likely come off the bench on Saturday and look to provide a spark in Game 7.

 Payton Pritchard tallied 32 points (12-of-21 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and six three-pointers in Sunday’s Game 4 win over the 76ers. 
 On a day when starter Derrick White (6/6/3/1/2 with two three-pointers) attempted just five shots, Pritchard stepped up with one of the best outings of his postseason career. The 32 points, a playoff career-high for Pritchard, were two shy of the Celtics franchise record for most in a playoff game by a reserve, which Kevin McHale still holds. While he made too many starts to qualify for NBA Sixth Man of the Year honors, Pritchard remains one of the best reserve scorers in the league. And he reminded Philadelphia of that in Game 4. The Celtics will look to close out the series on Tuesday night.

 All of Pritchard’s 15 points came on his five three-pointers. None were bigger than the one to beat the shot clock and put the Celtics up by five with less than a minute and a half remaining in regulation. Pritchard was +16 in 33 minutes on the night.

 Payton Pritchard (foot), Sam Hauser (back) and Nikola Vučević (finger) are doubtful for Sunday’s game against the Magic. 
 The Celtics, who secured the No. 2 seed in the East with Friday’s win over the Pelicans, will sit most of their key rotation players on Sunday. Pritchard and Hauser not playing would free up additional minutes for some of Boston’s rarely used perimeter reserves, including Ron Harper Jr. As for Vučević, his absence would open a spot in the rotation for Amari Williams.

 Payton Pritchard had 21 points (7-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, 10 assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Pelicans. 
 Pritchard came off the bench, but led the Celtics with 30 minutes played. The 28-year-old point guard had 21 points on 14 attempts from the field, five three-pointers and 10 assists. Pritchard provided seventh-round per game value this season. After another great year, he’s a candidate to sit out the Celtics’ last game on Sunday since they’ve now clinched the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference.

 CJ McCollum lit up the Rockets with 20 points (8-of-16 FGs), one rebound, three assists, three steals and four three-pointers on Monday.
 McCollum has been a solid source of offense for the Hawks since they traded for him last season. So far this year, his production has been underwhelming, but this ended up being his best scoring performance of the season. He has been efficient as a scorer, but the lack of volume has prevented him from making much of an impact for fantasy managers. Still, as a starter, he’ll continue to produce standard-league value.

 Dillon Brooks finished Monday’s loss to the Thunder with 19 points (4-of-14 FGs, 8-of-12 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and three three-pointers.
 Brooks didn’t have a good night shooting the basketball, making three of his ten three-point attempts and going 4-of-14 overall. The good news is that he recorded a complete stat line, which is welcome for a player whose fantasy value has underwhelmed so far. Brooks’ 2025-26 output factored into his preseason ADP, as he exceeded many fantasy managers’ expectations last season.

 Isaiah Hartenstein accounted for 15 points (6-of-7 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), 13 rebounds and three assists in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 With Chet Holmgren (knee) sitting out Monday’s game, Hartenstein was the lone 7-footer in the Thunder starting lineup. He recorded his second double-double in as many nights, and iHart’s ability to play both games of Oklahoma City’s back-to-back is encouraging. He appeared in 47 games last season, and injuries also contributed to Hartenstein’s minutes dropping by more than three per game. He’s looked healthy so far, which is critical with the Thunder losing Jalen Williams (ankle/leg) for the season on Sunday.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Monday’s win over the Suns with 26 points (11-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one three-pointer.
 In the aftermath of the injuries to Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams, some may have expected Gilgeous-Alexander to shoot until his arm fell off. That didn’t happen, as the reigning MVP got his points while also trusting his teammates. SGA recorded just three assists, but he shot the ball well and extended his 20-point streak to 143 games. Oklahoma City plays two more games in Week 2, starting with the Mavericks on Wednesday.

 Jared McCain tallied 18 points (6-of-14 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 McCain was one of three replacements in the Thunder starting lineup on Monday. With Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/leg) needing surgery, McCain has a good chance of staying a starter for the long haul. He shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc against the Suns and recorded a complete stat line, playing 30 minutes. Like Ajay Mitchell, McCain is a must-add if he’s on the waiver wire.

 Ajay Mitchell went off for 30 points (10-of-16 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 With Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/leg) out for the foreseeable future, the Thunder will need greater contributions from players like Mitchell to stay afloat in the West. The third-year guard started on Monday and delivered the best game of his NBA career to date. Mitchell finished with his first 30-point game and was a steal shy of a complete stat line. If Mitchell is still on your league’s waiver wire, add him immediately.
